newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Competition soon in Israeli international telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Competition soon in Israeli international telecoms.

text.p: Competition in Israel's market for international telephone calls, which was to begin on July 1, will start up within a few days, Communications Minister Limor Livnat said on Wednesday.

"International competition was due to have started yesterday, the day in which dialling rates were supposed to drop substantially as a result of the introduction of two new companies into the market," Livnat told Israel Radio.
"We are talking of a delay of only a few days," she added.
The delay resulted from a dispute with Bezeq Israel Telecom over dialling rates.

Livnat accused state-owned Bezeq of violating the law and exploiting its dominant market position after the company published proposed international tariffs as much as 80 percent below current rates without ministry approval.
Livnat said Bezeq's international phone service subsidiary was offering customers "dumping prices" and asked Israel's anti-trust authority to intervene.

"Every citizen can ask themselves how it can be that Bezeq International can offer such cheap prices after we paid much higher prices all these years...this is the difference between a monopoly and competition," Livnat said.
She also said Bezeq workers were refusing to connect the two new providers, Barak and Golden Lines.
"That is of course an illegal activity which we will deal with," she said.

Under the law, Bezeq is subject to strict supervision during the first six months of the new competitive market. Bezeq said the ministry knew of its ad campaign and that it had not violated the law because the new rates were not yet in force.
Golden Lines is owned by SBC Communications Inc, Italy's Stet and three Israeli partners.
Barak is owned by Sprint Corp, France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom, Clal Israel and Matav Cable Systems Media Ltd.
Livnat said that as a result of the competition a call to the Unites States will drop from around 3.50 shekels a minute to 0.70-0.80 shekels.
